drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main problem: fatigue, weight change, thirst, heat or cold intolerance, neck swelling, tremor, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main endocrine complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: When did this start, and is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Tempo helps separate acute metabolic decompensation from gradual thyroid or adrenal disease.

questions.text: How tired are you, and does rest help, or is it a new crushing fatigue?
questions.rationale: Endocrine disease often presents as unexplained fatigue.

questions.text: Have you gained or lost weight without trying, and about how much?
questions.rationale: Unintended weight change is a core thyroid, diabetes, and adrenal clue.

questions.text: Are you much thirstier than usual, peeing a lot, or getting up often at night to pee?
questions.rationale: Polyuria and polydipsia suggest new or uncontrolled diabetes.

questions.text: Have you had very high or very low blood sugar, confusion, vomiting, or deep rapid breathing?
questions.rationale: Hyperglycemia with vomiting or Kussmaul breathing can be DKA; severe hypoglycemia is an emergency.

questions.text: Do you feel unusually hot or cold when others do not, or have you noticed sweating or dry skin?
questions.rationale: Heat and cold intolerance help separate hyperthyroidism from hypothyroidism.

questions.text: Do you have a racing heart, shakiness, or feeling wired?
questions.rationale: These features support thyrotoxicosis or hypoglycemia.

questions.text: Have you noticed a swelling or lump in the front of your neck, or trouble swallowing?
questions.rationale: A goiter or nodule may accompany thyroid dysfunction or mass effect.

questions.text: Are your eyes prominent, gritty, or do you have double vision?
questions.rationale: Orbitopathy points toward Graves disease.

questions.text: Has your hair thinned, or has your skin become very dry, coarse, or darker in creases?
questions.rationale: Hair and skin changes occur with thyroid, androgen, and adrenal disease.

questions.text: Have your periods changed, or has your sex drive or erections changed?
questions.rationale: Hypogonadism and thyroid disease often show up in reproductive symptoms.

questions.text: Have you had dizziness on standing, salt craving, unexplained vomiting, or a very dark tan without sun?
questions.rationale: These features raise concern for adrenal insufficiency, which can decompensate quickly.

questions.text: Have you taken steroid pills, injections, or high-dose inhalers, especially if you stopped suddenly?
questions.rationale: Abrupt steroid cessation can precipitate adrenal crisis.

questions.text: Have you had kidney stones, constipation, extra thirst, or bone pain?
questions.rationale: These can reflect hypercalcemia or parathyroid disease.

questions.text: Do you get muscle cramps, tingling around your mouth, or spasms in your hands?
questions.rationale: Neuromuscular irritability can indicate hypocalcemia.

questions.text: Have you been told you have diabetes, prediabetes, or high blood sugar?
questions.rationale: Known diabetes frames hypoglycemia, DKA, and complication screening.

questions.text: Have you had thyroid disease, thyroid surgery, or radioactive iodine?
questions.rationale: Prior thyroid treatment explains current hypo- or hyperthyroid symptoms.

questions.text: Does anyone in your family have thyroid disease, diabetes, or other hormone problems?
questions.rationale: Family history raises likelihood of autoimmune endocrine disease.

questions.text: Do you have headaches, vision loss, or milky nipple discharge?
questions.rationale: These can indicate a pituitary mass or hyperprolactinemia.

questions.text: Are you taking insulin, thyroid hormone, steroids, or any new medicines?
questions.rationale: Dosing errors in hormone medicines commonly cause new symptoms.

questions.text: Have you had a recent infection, surgery, or been unable to take your usual hormone medicines?
questions.rationale: Intercurrent illness precipitates DKA and adrenal crisis.

questions.text: How is this affecting your work, sleep, or daily activities?
questions.rationale: Functional impact guides urgency.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Possible DKA or severe hypoglycemia
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report very high or low blood sugar with confusion, vomiting, or deep rapid breathing?

red_flags.label: Possible adrenal crisis
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report dizziness on standing, vomiting, steroid stoppage, or a new dark tan with severe weakness?

red_flags.label: Possible severe hyperthyroidism
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report racing heart, tremor, heat intolerance, and feeling very unwell or confused?

red_flags.label: Headache with vision change or nipple discharge
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report headaches with vision loss or milky nipple discharge?

red_flags.label: Neck swelling with swallowing or breathing trouble
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a neck swelling with trouble swallowing or breathing?

red_flags.label: Severe thirst and urination
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report marked thirst, very frequent urination, and feeling dehydrated or confused?
